- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast shows strong upward bias, apply downward correction by 3–5% to prevent false optimism.
- Model tends to overestimate short-term volatility in high-sentiment periods — dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day moving average.
- In low-sentiment periods, forecast mean reversion is often missed — adjust by adding 1–2% downward bias to avoid false continuation.
- When sentiment shifts sharply (e.g., from 0.6 to 0.0 or vice versa), delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid premature reaction.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment confirms sustained direction — use 2–3 day lagged sentiment to filter out noise.
